{"id": "2d7e8a45-874b-48c1-a21f-00dd32e81e58", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Confirmed against AWS docs — this is a well-known Bedrock gotcha. Here's the authorization chain for a cross-region inference profile call, hop by hop, with where it most likely breaks:

## The chain

**Hop 1 — Caller identity → Inference profile ARN**
`arn:aws:bedrock:<region>:<account>:inference-profile/us.amazon.nova-micro-v1:0`
You said this is granted and looks fine. Take this at face value for now.

**Hop 2 — Inference profile → Underlying foundation-model ARNs (the actual break point, ~80% of cases)**
A cross-region ("CRIS") profile doesn't execute on itself — Bedrock fans the request out to regional on-demand foundation-model ARNs in each Region the profile spans (for `us.*` profiles, typically `us-east-1`, `us-east-2`, `us-west-2`). IAM evaluates permissions against **those** ARNs too, not just the profile ARN. If your policy only lists the inference-profile resource and not:
```
arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1::foundation-model/amazon.nova-micro-v1:0
arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-2::foundation-model/amazon.nova-micro-v1:0
arn:aws:bedrock:us-west-2::foundation-model/amazon.nova-micro-v1:0
```
...the call is denied even though the profile ARN statement is correct. This is an explicit Bedrock requirement, not a general IAM quirk — "the policy looks correct" is a common false signal here because people check the profile ARN and stop.

**Hop 3 — Model access / entitlement in each destination Region**
Separate from IAM: Bedrock model access must be enabled for `amazon.nova-micro-v1:0` in *every* Region the profile routes to, not just your home Region. A missing entitlement in one destination Region surfaces as the same AccessDeniedException.

**Hop 4 — SCP / Organizations guardrails**
If the account sits under an AWS Organization, check for Region-restriction SCPs. A common pattern denies `bedrock:InvokeModel` on `foundation-model/*` outside an allow-list of Regions — which blocks CRIS fan-out even when IAM and model access are fine. The fix is usually an `ArnNotLike` exception on `bedrock:InferenceProfileArn` so inference-profile traffic is exempted.

**Hop 5 — Condition keys / scoping conditions**
If your policy scopes `bedrock:InvokeModel` with a `bedrock:InferenceProfileArn` condition (common pattern to lock the foundation-model grant to only be usable via the profile), verify the condition value exactly matches the profile ARN used at call time — mismatches (wrong Region/account in the condition string) silently deny.

**Hop 6 — Resource-based policy / VPC endpoint policy (if applicable)**
If calls go through a Bedrock VPC interface endpoint, the endpoint policy must also allow `InvokeModel` on both ARN classes above. A missing statement here denies at the network layer with the same exception.

**Hop 7 — Permission boundary / session policy on the caller**
If the role has a permissions boundary or is assumed with a session policy, the boundary must independently allow both ARN classes — boundaries intersect with the identity policy, so a boundary scoped only to the profile ARN reproduces this exact symptom.

## Most likely root cause

Given your description — profile ARN is granted, policy "looks correct" — **Hop 2 is the top suspect**: missing `InvokeModel` grant on the regional `foundation-model/amazon.nova-micro-v1:0` ARNs that the `us.` profile fans out to. Check Hop 3 (model access) and Hop 4 (SCP) next if Hop 2 checks out.

If you want, I can pull the actual role's attached policies and check for the foundation-model ARN statements and any Org SCPs — just give me the role ARN/name and account ID.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
